title: Worker rebuild fixtures use transport-safe local cloning and stop on setup failure before a worker round; clone diagnostics remain fixture-only and existing rebuild assertions stay intact
acceptance: Why. PR237 head9503609294202a92cc4f5198d1c2ca45f5d2e0aa run37722254605 job113132625772 fails X4 in tests/worker-executable.test.sh:77 after git local clone emits failed to copy loose object with ENOENT. Missing rebuild messages are consequences of absent fixture conflict, while round/executable assertions pass. Scope does not include production or T-254 reviewer-policy changes; captain dispatch approval and exact SPEC preflight precede implementation.

Known source, unknown race. tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh rb_move_main:112-117 clones local remote.git into other after removing other. rb_replay_conflict:147-155 calls it after task commits/push. tests/worker-executable.test.sh:75 ignores helper failure and runs round_two. Official git-clone documentation says local paths use local copy/hardlink optimization and concurrent source modification can race; --no-local uses ordinary transport (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone). The log proves clone ENOENT and unchecked setup failure, not whether source maintenance or destination deletion caused it. Do not claim confirmed gc or corruption.

Change 1. Use git clone --no-local -q -b main for rb_move_main fixture clones, keeping branch, source and destination unchanged. Local optimized clone is not a required behavior of rebuild tests. Report clone failure with a fixed fixture class and original Git error plus bounded fixture-only source/destination existence/ref information; no private external paths or live state. Return nonzero and never edit/push main when clone fails. Do not retry blindly or suppress the error. Fixed diagnostic prefix is rebuild fixture clone failed; original stderr tail is bounded to4KiB, added metadata uses local existence booleans and short ref IDs without absolute paths. Do not capture private live state. Added diagnostic text is private test evidence, never an external PR projection.

Change 2. Audit all consumers in tests/worker-executable.test.sh, worker-rebuild.test.sh, worker-rebuild-publication.test.sh and spec-pin-sync.test.sh. Guard every rb_move_main/rb_replay_conflict/rb_conflicting_main setup call that prepares a later round: a failure stops that fixture case before any worker invocation. Preserve intentional negative worker outcomes and all original rb_rebuilt/executable-bit assertions; fixture setup errors cannot masquerade as expected worker failures. Do not change rb_round_two production semantics or remove a case. Source helper callers are exactly these four shell suites at proposal time; recheck before implementation. Sweep nested setup wrappers, including rb_ascii_conflict in worker-rebuild.test.sh and initial X4 setup in worker-executable.test.sh. Failed initialization stops that case rather than echoing and continuing. Synthetic task commits may precede rb_move_main; the guarantee is no main mutation or worker invocation after clone failure, not zero earlier fixture effects.

Controlled proof. Add tests/worker-rebuild-fixture.test.sh. In isolated synthetic fixture state, a scoped git stub records argv, allows setup readers and makes only clone return128 with sentinel stderr; assert the helper returns nonzero, no main edit/push or worker round occurs, the fixed diagnostic identifies fixture clone failure, and original error remains. A second successful stub/real local bare fixture verifies --no-local selection and intended main change. Retain the harness and replace guarded caller with historical unchecked flow: assert worker-call sentinel appears and the no-worker-on-failed-setup case turns red. This proves failure control flow, not the unproven disappearing-object mechanism. Preserve stdout/return contracts of helpers on success. Add test-only RB_FIXTURE_LIBRARY_ONLY=1 guards solely around eager rb_build_fixture calls and rb_add temporary initializer in the complete worker-rebuild.sh helper; all four existing suites keep default eager setup unchanged. The new controlled wrapper sources the entire helper in this library-only mode, owns synthetic paths/cleanup and stubs only clone failure; no truncated source extraction. Historical proof overlays only these test-library initializer guards and the complete harness on recorded base while restoring original clone/caller behavior, so failed no-worker/transport assertions are behavioral and do not accidentally launch unrelated eager rounds.

Fail-first and regression. All real PR changes are tests/**; ordinary fail-first retains changed tests and has no runtime implementation to revert. Label this honestly. A historical-base experiment overlays the complete new harness on a recorded accepted base with original helper/caller behavior, injects the deterministic clone failure and records the worker-call sentinel/no-guard assertion failure; no absent-helper import-error proof. Run unchanged rebuild/X4 semantics with successful fixture setup through CI/gates; relevant full four suites remain regression coverage. No larger sleeps, timeout weakening, production edits, CI skips or retry-as-success.

Migration/design/privacy. No runtime record, config, branch policy, pin or design contract changes. New wrapper is auto-discovered by CI; no production workflow change. Fixtures are synthetic/private to the temporary test root, inherit no live project/HERDR routing and cleanup only owned fixture resources. Keep new diagnostics bounded. Workers do not run suites; firstmate/CI/gates retain actual final-head results. If later evidence proves a production clone issue, request separate approved scope first.

Split audit migration. Update only tests/worker.test.sh entry scaffolding exemptions in tests/lib/split-manifest.json using existing line/count/reason objects for actual replaced clone/setup/caller lines and exact removed multiplicity. Keep historical base and files list unchanged; never exempt assert_*, test names, assertion messages or reduce inventory counts. Document each replacement as T261 transport-safe clone or setup-failure guard. New tests/worker-rebuild-fixture.test.sh remains outside the historical split file inventory and supplies additional feature coverage. Run unchanged python3 tests/lib/split_audit.py (existing direct audit entry point) to prove all original assertions/names/counts and remaining non-comment lines survive. No split_audit.py scanner/schema weakening or general replacement rule.
